questions.q: Who is most likely to lose from unexpected inflation?
options: Savers on low fixed interest rates
questions.why: Their money buys less, and the interest doesn't make up for it.

questions.q: What matters most for international competitiveness?
options: UK inflation compared with inflation abroad
The size of the UK's money supply alone
questions.why: What counts is whether UK prices rise faster than rivals' prices.

options: Consumers delay spending, expecting lower prices
questions.why: This can start a deflationary spiral.

questions.q: A fall in prices caused by rising productivity can be good for an economy.
questions.why: It comes from the supply side, with no fall in demand.

questions.q: A sharp rise in world oil prices would cause what kind of UK inflation?
questions.why: Firms' costs rise, because of events abroad.

questions.q: Explain why deflation can be especially harmful to an economy with high levels of debt.

ideas.label: Debts stay the same while prices and incomes fall, so the real burden rises
So borrowers cut spending, which lowers AD

questions.model: Debts stay the same in money terms while prices and incomes fall, so the real burden rises. Borrowers cut back on spending, which lowers AD.
questions.why: Debts don't shrink when wages do.

tests.answer: The real burden of debt rises, so people spend less and AD falls.
